messages:
eli: Heads-up — SpectralFintech just sent back the RFI with two new asks: per-route token cost breakdown and an audit-retention table for the POC. I uploaded a draft capability matrix.
priya: link to the draft?
eli: sales-ops-bot uploaded: 1789456123-spectralfin-rfi-draft.xlsx
tony: Quick technical: they want a recommended quantization + latency tradeoffs for 7B/13B. We should call out KV-cache behavior in the matrix.
samir: short answer: for throughput-focused POC, recommend int8 (q4/q5) with KV cache enabled. Typical numbers:
```
Model            | Quant  | Latency delta | Cost delta
redwood-7b-q4    | int8   | +12%          | -48%
redwood-13b-q5   | int8   | +18%          | -52%
fallback-hosted  | fp16   | 0%            | +110%
```
samir: I'll paste a one-paragraph explanation for the RFI too.
priya: Legal flagged bring-your-own-HSM + attestation as a hard blocker for their security team. @marie can we scope a connector or an approved workaround for the POC?
marie: We can support a VPC HSM connector for the Private deployment POC but it will add time. ETA: approx 3-4 weeks to implement and validate attestation flows. We'll need a contract amendment for any HSM-backed POC.
eli: Noted. Customer also asked for a POC price cap. Proposed commercial: $5k/week, up to 100k tokens/day, and we limit model family to 7B/13B for the duration. Any objections?
tony: That seems reasonable if we lock model variants and provide fallback routing to hosted during spikes. Add a line in the matrix about canary/fallback behavior.
priya: I'll confirm the cap with the customer today. Once they accept, we need legal redline from @marie and an ops runbook from infra.
samir: I'll update the capability matrix and attach the updated PDF with quant/latency rows and the RFI writeup by EOD.
eli: Action items: priya confirm price cap to customer; marie produce amendment draft; samir/tony update matrix and ops notes. :thumbsup:
priya: on it
marie: drafting amendment now
sales-ops-bot uploaded: 1789456399-spectralfin-capability-matrix-v2.pdf
